These four greetings are written صَبَاحَ الْخَيْر / صَبَاحَ النُّور with an accusative -a. Everywhere else the course teaches the nominative صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر / صَبَاحُ النُّور (109 times), and the learner sees and hears the inconsistency (ṣabāḥa l-khayr).

أَيّ is the interrogative heading the nominal clause أَيُّهُمَا لِلْوَرَقَة ('which of the two is for the note'). The verb أَعْرِفُ is suspended (taʿlīq), so أَيّ is a mubtadaʾ in the nominative: أَيُّهُمَا. The accusative أَيَّهُمَا is wrong for this syntax.

This dialogue spells wallet مَحْفَظَة (وَمَحْفَظَتِي, الْمَحْفَظَة), but the rest of the course, including the machines scenario and the vocabulary, uses مِحْفَظَة. Both forms exist, but the learner gets two vocalisations of the same core word.
errors.alsoChange: segs وَمَحْفَظَتِي / الْمَحْفَظَة → وَمِحْفَظَتِي / الْمِحْفَظَة; transliteration follows

notes.note: The photo is of the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, but the scenario takes place at the Jordan Museum in Amman.
The photo is of Jordan Post in Amman, but the dialogue is at a Cairo post office (Egypt Post).
The caption says the tourist police are at Petra, but the story is in downtown Amman.
السَّقْف is tapped as 'the ceiling' while the English says 'the roof'. Either word is fine, but they should match.
The ticket seller uses the dual (تُرِيدَانِ أَنْ تَجْلِسَا) to Daniel, who is alone at the window. It is defensible because he buys two tickets, but it may surprise learners.
سَأَتَأَكَّدُ مِنَ الطَّبَّاخِ literally means 'I will make sure of the cook'. سَأَسْأَلُ الطَّبَّاخَ بِنَفْسِي or سَأَتَأَكَّدُ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ مَعَ الطَّبَّاخِ would be clearer.
The story logic is odd: the machine 'took the twenty-pound note from my wallet'. 'Took my twenty-pound note' would be clearer.
The intro presents تَفَضَّلْ as 'please, go ahead', but the tap shows 'here you are (to a man)'. This is not wrong, but it does not match the sense being taught.

summary: I read the whole scenarios-2 chunk: 16 scenarios (airport-checkin to school), with their dialogues, segs, mistake cards and quizzes, plus their scene photo spots. I checked harakat and case, agreement, verb moods after an/lan/lam/lā, number–noun rules (3–10 polarity, 11–99 tamyīz, hundreds), the totals in the dialogues against the quiz keys, and every tap gloss. The dialogue Arabic is in very good shape: number agreement, dual forms, moods and the gender of address are correct throughout, and all quiz answer keys and mistake-card rules are right. I found 17 errors (3 major, 14 minor). The majors are all tap glosses: شَرِيحَة/شَرَائِح is glossed as 'slide' in the SIM-card scenario (two findings), and the correct mistake card's أَفْضَلُ is glossed as 'the best'. The minors are mostly tap glosses that take a sense from another context: مِنْ 'from' for 'than', الْمَكْتَب 'office' for counter or desk, الْعَرَبَة 'carriage', هُوَ 'he' for 'it', سَيِّدَات 'toilets', the tourist-police hints. The others are an inconsistent accusative صَبَاحَ الْخَيْر in two scenarios, أَيَّهُمَا for أَيُّهُمَا, an inconsistent مَحْفَظَة/مِحْفَظَة, a ẕ typo, and one engine issue: tanwīn before waṣla is rendered 'taqrīran l-āna' instead of 'taqrīrani l-āna'. Tap glosses checked: 818 word glosses on 366 tap lines; 23 of them are wrong or misleading in their line (all covered by the gloss findings above).
